classification.difficultyReason: Infer from the inscribed configuration that the cone's radius and perpendicular height both equal r, then form and simplify the ratio of cone volume to hemisphere volume.

content.prompt: A cone is inscribed in a hemisphere of radius $r$. What fraction of the hemisphere is taken up by the cone?

spec.description: Hemisphere with an inscribed cone sharing its circular base and reaching its highest point; base radius labelled r. Decorative cyan fill omitted under house style. Rear base arc is dashed to distinguish hidden geometry.
spec.mathematics: The cone has base radius r and perpendicular height r.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius is labelled; no calculated volume or fraction is shown.

answer.worked:
The cone has radius $r$ and height $r$.
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cone}}&=\frac13\pi r^2(r)\\V_{\text{cone}}&=\frac13\pi r^3\\V_{\text{hemisphere}}&=\frac23\pi r^3\\\frac{V_{\text{cone}}}{V_{\text{hemisphere}}}&=\frac{\frac13\pi r^3}{\frac23\pi r^3}\\\frac{V_{\text{cone}}}{V_{\text{hemisphere}}}&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
